title: CORNER Vision Page Spec
summary: Spec for corner.app/vision: the public roadmap page. Shows where Corner is going without revealing proprietary timelines. Builds investor and client confidence. Heaven design language.
content:
CORNER Vision Page: The Roadmap as a Page

Author: Steve (AI Advisory Lead) Date: 2026-03-16 For: Steffen (design) + Bobby (implementation) URL: corner.app/vision

Purpose

This page answers the question every investor, prospect, and curious developer asks: "Where is this going?"

The page is NOT a detailed spec. It's a narrative. A story told in 7 chapters. Each chapter gets a title, a one-liner, and a handful of bullet points. The page feels like reading a novel's chapter summaries. You can see the arc. You can feel the ambition. You want to keep reading.

Who reads this page:

  • Investors evaluating the vision
  • Enterprise prospects evaluating long-term viability
  • Developers deciding whether to build on the platform
  • Press writing about Corner
  • Job candidates evaluating whether to join

What this page does NOT do:

  • Reveal specific timelines (no dates, no quarter estimates)
  • Commit to features (language is "we're building toward" not "we will ship")
  • Show internal architecture or technical details
  • Replace the demo or product page (this is the why, not the how)

Page Structure

Section 1: Hero

Layout: Full viewport. White background. Massive headline. Minimal.

Headline:

This is a 10-year company.

64-72px. Weight 600. Centered. Breathes.

Subheadline:

Corner started as an AI assistant for one business.
Here's what it becomes.

18-20px. Weight 400. Color: #666. Max-width: 480px.

No CTA in the hero. This page is for reading, not converting. CTAs come at the bottom.

Section 2: The Chapters

Layout: Vertical scroll. Each chapter is a full-width section. Alternating background: white (#FFFFFF) and near-white (#FAFAFA). Heavy whitespace between sections.

Each chapter card contains:

  • Chapter number (large, decorative: "C3", "C4", etc.)
  • Chapter name (24-32px, bold)
  • One-liner (16-18px, the thesis in a sentence)
  • 4-6 bullet points (the features, simplified for a non-technical audience)
  • A small isometric illustration that represents the chapter's theme (Steffen designs)

The chapter number is the visual anchor. Big. Bold. Maybe in the accent color. It creates rhythm as you scroll: C3, C4, C5, C6, C7, C8, C9.

Chapter Cards Content

C3: The Living Office Your AI team comes to life.

  • Agents move, think, and work in real-time
  • Chat with any agent directly
  • Three ways to see everything: the game, the checklist, the stats
  • Works on your phone, your laptop, anywhere

C4: The Hosted Product Anyone can have one.

  • Sign up and your office is ready in under a minute
  • Your data is yours. Completely isolated. Bank-level security.
  • AOM manages everything behind the scenes
  • Updates happen automatically. Your agents get smarter over time.

C5: The Sticky Platform A world you build and never want to leave.

  • Customize your office. Furniture, themes, layout.
  • Skills marketplace: teach your agents new tricks
  • Track your ROI. See exactly what your agents save you.
  • Connect with other Corner offices

C6: The Ecosystem Others build on it. Others sell it.

  • Developer SDK: build apps on top of Corner
  • Voice: talk to your agents, hear them respond
  • Available in every language
  • Partners and agencies resell Corner under their own brand

C7: The Intelligence Layer It learns. It predicts. It teaches.

  • Corner Academy: learn AI operations from your own data
  • Teams: multiple people in one office, working with different agents
  • Industry editions: built specifically for your trade
  • Predictive insights: Corner tells you what's coming before you ask

C8: The Operating System Corner runs your whole business.

  • Files, communication, finance, HR, legal. All in one place.
  • Dedicated hardware: always-on screen on your desk
  • AI-native CRM: your agents already know every client interaction
  • A network of businesses connected through their agents

C9: The Autonomous Company The system runs itself.

  • Self-building AI: describe your business, Corner builds your entire team
  • A marketplace of talent: find specialists through the network
  • Financial services: Corner knows your business well enough to fund it
  • Global: Corner in every market, every language, every industry

Section 3: The Through-Line

Layout: Full viewport. White background. Centered text. This is the narrative section.

Each chapter builds on the last.

C3 makes it real.
C4 makes it available.
C5 makes it yours.
C6 makes it an ecosystem.
C7 makes it smart.
C8 makes it the operating system.
C9 makes it self-sustaining.

The product starts as a tool.
Becomes a world.
Becomes infrastructure.
Becomes the way business works.

Typography: Each line on its own. Large (20-24px). Weight 400. Color fades from #333 (top) to #999 (bottom) as the vision extends further. Or: all the same weight, just let the whitespace do the work.

Section 4: What's Live Now

Layout: Two columns (desktop). Stacked (mobile).

Left column: "What works today"

  • A curated list of what's already shipped or in active build
  • Not everything. Just enough to show this isn't vaporware.
  • Example: "Real-time agents. Three viewing modes. Mobile app. Skills system. AI audit onboarding."

Right column: "What's next"

  • The next chapter being built (C3 at launch)
  • 3-4 bullet points of what's coming
  • No timeline. Just "this is what we're working on right now."

This section grounds the vision in reality. Without it, the page feels like a fantasy. With it, the page feels like a plan.

Section 5: Bottom CTA

Layout: Full viewport. Clean. Two paths.

For business owners:

Ready to meet your AI team?
[Start Free Trial]

For developers:

Want to build on this?
[Developer Portal]

For investors / press:

Want to talk?
hello@aom-inhouse.com

Three links. Three audiences. Simple.

Design Notes for Steffen

Illustrations

Each chapter needs one isometric illustration. Small. Contained. These aren't hero images. They're accents. Think: a tiny corner of a world, floating in whitespace.

C3: A small office with agents moving. One speech bubble visible. C4: Multiple tiny offices, separated, each self-contained. A hand placing one down. C5: An office bursting with furniture, personality. Stars/XP floating above. C6: Multiple offices connected by thin lines. A speech waveform over one. C7: An office with a brain/neural icon glowing above it. A crystal ball on the desk. C8: A full campus. Multiple buildings. A small city. C9: The campus running itself. No human avatar visible. Just agents, working.

Typography

This page is the most type-heavy page on the site. The typography must be impeccable.

  • Chapter numbers: the display font, at 48-64px, in the accent color
  • Chapter names: the body font, at 24-32px, weight 600
  • One-liners: italicized, 18-20px, weight 400
  • Bullets: 16px, weight 400, generous line height (1.8)
  • Through-line section: the display font, 20-24px, weight 400

Animation

Slow. Chapters fade in as you scroll. Each chapter appears ~300ms after the previous one if they're all in view. If scrolling, each chapter fades up as it enters the viewport (IntersectionObserver, 0.2 threshold, 600ms ease-in).

The through-line section: each line fades in sequentially, 200ms stagger. Not fast. A meditation pace.

Bobby's Implementation Notes

  • This is a static page. No dynamic content.
  • Add to the marketing site nav under "Company" dropdown or as a standalone nav item.
  • MDX if the content might change often. Hardcoded if it's stable.
  • Performance: no heavy assets. Text + tiny SVG/PNG illustrations. Should be the lightest page on the site.
  • SEO: "Corner AI Roadmap", "Corner Vision", "Corner Product Roadmap". Good for people searching "Corner AI future" or "Corner AI roadmap."

When to Ship

Ship this page with the marketing site launch (C3). It's a credibility page. When Patrik sends a link to an investor or enterprise prospect, this is one of the first pages they'll visit. "What are you building?" "Go to corner.app/vision."

Update the page quarterly. Add "shipped" tags to completed chapters. Move the "what's next" section forward. The page is a living document that shows progress over time.

This page doesn't sell anything. It earns trust. The visitor reads it and thinks: "These people know exactly what they're building. They've thought this through. I want to be part of this." That's the conversion. Not a signup. A conviction.
